notes.title: August Community Update - Feedback Welcome
notes.content:
Hi everyone. It’s been about a month since we announced The Run: Got Next and we’re thrilled with the reception so far. We’re taking that excitement to continue to push us as we make more progress on the game. To that point, we wanted to share some of what we’ve been working on behind the scenes and areas where we're welcoming feedback.

[b]Differentiating Teams[/b]
Because we’re a street based game, we don’t currently intend on having players in matching uniforms (plus, we feel it would take away from the character’s personalities). We’re looking right now at Shirts vs. Skins, with some additional variances. Not only is this easy to read visually, but it’s also how things often play out in pickup games. (Note: we will also have UI elements to help distinguish you and your teammates).

Here’s a quick screenshot our Creative Director took in early exploration of shirts and skins.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45117598/9a30465f45cac176957bb8c61e81c9b3d1625c6a.png[/img]

[b]Courts[/b] 
If you’ve made it here, you’ve no doubt seen our recreation of the Tenement Court we showed in our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vmq1zu8u0OU]teaser trailer[/url] from the Philippines. This month, we’ve been steadily improving the look of that court and others. And now that we have a quality bar set, we’re moving onto additional courts not only for launch, but also for post-launch. Are there any courts you want to see? 

Here’s a very (very) early look at a court hoops fans should be able to ID right away.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45117598/c7a8bd003cc117eae17af19a30ffaa576ac54437.png[/img]

[b]Courts Influencing Gameplay[/b]
Another idea related to courts we’re exploring is how to make sure each one can feel distinctive. We’re being very intentional on which courts we’re choosing so we have a good variety. And we want them to influence gameplay in an authentic way that will require you to think strategically about your lineups. As we recreate different courts, we’ll be considering things that are unique – from court size, rims, 3pt distance, surroundings, weather and more. 

We’ve been seeing some awesome examples in the real world of courts with a 4 point line, courts where [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4sDFWqseEgw&t=584s] large overhanging tree branches[/url] are an obstacle for long range shots, courts where fans always seem to get a little too close to the action. Let us know if you have any thoughts on how courts and their environments should impact gameplay. 

[b]Have Opinions? Join our Discord[/b]
If you want to stay up to date with what the development team is doing and see more behind the scenes and (sometimes extremely) work in progress visuals from the team, you should join our [url=https://discord.gg/FTVScM3M]Discord[/url]. Not only do we do our best to share weekly updates on Friday’s, we ask for specific feedback. If you have opinions, we want to hear them. 

As a small team in a brand new studio, all of us at Play by Play want to cultivate a sense of connection with the community early on, especially for those of you who are already excited from our initial teaser. And we can’t wait to share more.

notes.title: Post Reveal - FAQ
notes.content:
Hello Steam community. We want to thank you for all of the excitement and support for [i][b]The Run: Got Next[/b][/i]. While our team has worked on a lot of big games, it's our first together as a studio, and we're looking forward to building it together with you.

That all starts with listening. So we thought our first post here on Steam should be answering some questions we've found from here and different corners of the internet. We may do this regularly on [url=https://discord.gg/GKpg929R]Discord[/url] and maybe here too. We'll see!

Thanks again, keep the feedback coming, and we'll see you on the court.

[b]So is this game half court? Full court? 3v3 only?[/b]
Our main mode is full court, 3v3. We’ve tested different scenarios, 2v2, even more players but 3v3 on a full court is the sweet spot for getting to the back and forth pace we think is most fun.

[b]How much is the game going to cost? Is it going to be free to play?[/b]
We’re still working that out right now, but rest assured our goal is to deliver a highly crafted game at a reasonable price. We’re not looking at Free to Play, it’s not the type of game we’re interested in making or the type of community we’re looking to build.

[b]Why didn’t you show gameplay? When will I see gameplay?[/b]
When we show gameplay, we really want you to see the full experience of The Run – more characters, how The Run system works, the roguelike elements, you haven’t even heard about hype mode yet… But at least we didn’t ask you to pre-order, right? ;)

[b]What about monetization? Are you planning on selling items like other sports games?[/b]
One of our principles is to make sure players won’t have to waste their time (or money) ripping packs to be able to compete and have fun. This is a video game, not a casino. We want you to jump in, have a blast and enjoy your time in The Run right from the get go playing basketball. There will be things we sell at some point after launch, but they’re more cosmetic and new content oriented in nature. More to come.

[b]Can the game be played offline?[/b]
No, the game is fully PvP. You’ll be able to play by yourself or in a squad of up to 3 players against other teams online.

[b]If I ask more and more about a true single player mode, will you make it?[/b]
Maybe, eventually? We’re focusing on nailing an amazing game, and we’ve got our hands full with ensuring the online experience works as intended, but we’re definitely listening to everything the community is saying. 

[b]Are you planning on giving players a chance to playtest before launch?[/b]
Absolutely! As a new studio, it’s especially important for us to get players into the game early in order to collect feedback and to make sure our online systems are working as intended. We’ll have more to say on this later as we’re getting closer.

[b]Why aren’t you making a straight re-master of NBA Street, Vol 2?[/b]
Street and games like that are definitely the inspiration. But we also want to make something that introduces some of the fun elements from different genres we all have loved playing since Street. 

[b]Aren’t you guys part of EA?[/b]
A lot of our team used to work at EA, many of us for 10+ years. We’ve also got team members who have worked at Riot, Epic, Crystal Dynamics and some members who come from outside games too. We are fully independent, our own, small team – about a dozen, and we have some key partners as well.

[b]Will there be couch co-op?[/b]
We loved playing games like Street on the couch and we definitely are seeing you all feel the same! It’s something we’ll investigate but we can’t confirm anything right now.

[b]How are you thinking about live service?[/b]
We definitely have a lot of ideas on content we can add – new courts, characters, game modes. Our approach and focus right now is on launching the game first and making it as great as it can be. And of course, one of the biggest reasons we want to see this community grow is to talk to players and understand what they’re looking for in live – courts, characters, features, etc. Fire away!

[b]Is the game going to have any NBA players?[/b]
Right now we’re focused on creating our own roster of characters to make sure you have a diverse group of playstyles to choose from right from launch. But it’s something we’re definitely open to and we think there are ways to include players and really anyone who is authentic to the sport of basketball into our world and game, which we as players would be excited about. If you have any ideas, please feel free to share. 

[b]What about other sports? The footballs? Hockey? Baseball?[/b]
We're focusing on basketball right now, making sure we nail it and get it right. But absolutely we think this formula can work for other sports and have ideas. It’s one of the reasons we started the company, we think the whole genre can use some new energy.

notes.title: Former NBA Street devs are looking to do what EA won't - new studio to make spiritual successor to fan favourite
notes.content:
Former NBA Street developers from EA have broken off from the video game giant to form their own studio and create a spiritual successor to the beloved basketball game. The game, titled The Run: Got Next, will be developed at the brand-new Play by Play Studios. The game itself is set to release in 2025 for Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

Speaking to IGN on the game's reveal, co-founder of Play by Play Studios and former Madden creative director Mike Young talked about the developer's attitude towards the NBA Street Legacy, "There was a lot of us that worked on NBA Street that always wanted to bring it back. I think it is difficult for a company that has a game like a Madden or an NBA Live that is so big. If you're putting all your resources to that, I think it was challenging to think about a secondary game," Young says.

"I was there when the Tiburon Studio brought back [NFL Blitz]. Some of the things I've seen in the past, they're just nostalgia plays and they kind of haven't evolved to a modern game. I think they don't have staying power, so they have to come out at a smaller price point. You may only attract the people who liked them, and then they play it for a weekend or a couple of weeks or bring it out every once in a while..."
